flags: Follow-up needed: unlock approved (APR-0003) but the change failed to apply. Ticket INC0010021 is still on_hold and the caller remains locked out — on-call technician must complete the unlock and update the ticket today.
Caller was told to 'watch for a text' about INC0010021, so the promised update must actually be sent.
coaching: When the caller says they're done ('No, that's everything. Thank you!'), skip the full recap and close with one short sentence — the recap repeated the previous turn almost word for word.

Combine the verification-code narration into a single sentence ('I'm texting a six-digit code to your mobile on file ending in 0115 — please read it back') instead of announcing it twice back to back.

Make the read-back phrasing more natural: 'unlocking your account, which is for being locked out after too many sign-in attempts' is clunky — e.g. 'unlocking your account after too many sign-in attempts'.

strengths: Fast and effortless for the caller: verified, confirmed, and handed off in 30 seconds, with Ananya never having to repeat herself.
Numbers were said in a speakable way throughout ('I N C 1 0 0 1 4', 'ending in 0 1 1 5'), and the agent used her first name and stayed warm.
When the unlock failed, the agent apologised plainly and gave clear next steps: 'A technician will finish it and update ticket I N C 1 0 0 2 1, so please watch for a text.'
issues: The closing recap repeated the previous turn almost word for word ('your unlock request was approved, but the change didn't complete...') right after the caller said 'No, that's everything. Thank you!' — a shorter goodbye would have respected her time.
The code step was narrated twice back to back: 'I'll text a six-digit code...' immediately followed by 'A code has been texted...' — one combined sentence would have been smoother.
The read-back phrasing was slightly clunky: 'unlocking your account, which is for being locked out after too many sign-in attempts' — understandable but not natural speech.
experience.summary: A quick, kind, and clear call where Ananya was verified and her unlock handed to a technician in 30 seconds, held back only by a redundant final recap and some doubled narration.

scorecard.headline: Yuki Tanaka's Zoom microphone issue couldn't be fixed live after she stopped engaging with the troubleshooting steps, so with her explicit confirmation the agent logged INC0010022 (P3) and promised technician follow-up. Handling was clean and rule-compliant throughout, though the agent re-asked the same microphone-menu question five times before offering the ticket.
coaching: When a caller gives two consecutive non-answers (e.g. 'Okay') to a troubleshooting step, stop re-asking the same question: switch to a simple yes/no check, verify the line is working, or offer to log a ticket. The agent repeated essentially the same microphone-menu question five times (17s-32s) before offering the ticket at 36s.

Ask one question per turn during guided troubleshooting. Double questions like 'Did the arrow menu show a microphone list, and is the one you're using selected?' are hard to answer on a phone call, especially for a minimally responsive caller.
Use caller-friendly wording in ticket read-backs: say 'standard priority' rather than the internal-sounding 'priority 3'.

strengths: Stayed calm, warm and patient despite getting only 'Okay' five times in a row; never sounded annoyed and kept using the caller's name.
Honest and brief about the outage check: 'I couldn't reach the Zoom status page just now, so I can't confirm whether there's a wider problem, but let's work through it together.'

Good recovery and wrap-up: offered to log a ticket when troubleshooting stalled, read it back before submitting ('Is that right?'), gave the number slowly and speakably ('I N C 1 0 0 2 2'), and ended with a clear recap and next step ('A technician will follow up with you').
issues: Repeated essentially the same microphone-menu question five times (17s–32s) while the caller just said 'Okay'; it should have changed approach or offered the ticket after the second non-answer instead of re-asking.

Some turns asked two things at once, e.g. 'Did the arrow menu show a microphone list, and is the one you're using selected?' — hard to answer on a phone call, especially for a caller giving minimal responses.
'Priority 3' in the read-back is internal-sounding and means little to a caller; plainer wording like 'standard priority' would land better.
experience.summary: A polite, patient call with a clean ticket wrap-up, but dragged down by the agent re-asking the same troubleshooting question five times before offering an exit.
